_method: primary sources fetched live (AHDB wholesale dairy, ONS PPI, DESNZ quarterly energy prices, Defra egg stats); beef/energy/eggs/food-PPI verified but excluded as immaterial (<~10% y/y). Coffee is from Trading Economics quoting ICE futures — an aggregator, recorded as primary:false.

entries.title: UK wholesale butter down 46% year-on-year
entries.fact: UK wholesale butter averaged £3,320/tonne in the July 2026 reporting period (weeks 27-30, 29 June-26 July 2026), down 46% from £6,150/tonne a year earlier, per AHDB UK wholesale prices; bulk cream was down 45% and mild cheddar down 22% year-on-year in the same report.

quantification.how: AHDB UK wholesale butter price down 46% y/y to £3,320/tonne (from £6,150/tonne) as of the July 2026 reporting period (29 June-26 July 2026)

source.quote: Reporting period: Weeks 27-30 (29 June-26 July 2026). ... Butter | 3,320 | 350 | 3,240 | 2% | 6,150 | −46%

entries.angle: AHDB's July 2026 wholesale report puts butter at £3,320/tonne against £6,150 a year ago — a 46% fall on an input that dominates bakery, brunch and table-service menus. An opener can ask whether that drop is actually showing up in the group's dairy line, site by site.
entries.proof_pairing: COGS/GP% customer results — visibility of whether supplier pricing tracks the wholesale move
entries.caveats: Wholesale price, not contracted supplier price — groups on fixed dairy contracts may not see the fall yet. Butter also ticked up 2% month-on-month (+£80), so the short-term direction is up off the low. Vertical is a coarse proxy — prefer hand-matching to the account's actual menu. UK series (AHDB); do not apply to Ireland accounts. cost_down framing: this is margin relief the account may be leaving with suppliers — open as a visibility question, not a cost scare.

entries.title: Arabica coffee futures down 13% year-on-year
entries.fact: Arabica coffee futures (ICE) stood at 326.08 US cents/lb on 20 August 2026, 13.1% lower than a year earlier.

quantification.how: ICE arabica coffee futures at 326.08 USd/lb on 20 Aug 2026, 13.10% lower than a year ago (Trading Economics quoting ICE futures); GBP impact additionally depends on GBP/USD

source.quote: Coffee fell to 326.08 USd/Lbs on August 20, 2026 ... it is still 13.10% lower than a year ago.

entries.angle: Arabica futures sit at 326 US cents/lb as of 20 August 2026 — 13% below a year ago. For a coffee-led group, an opener can reference the easing green-bean market and whether roaster contract prices are following it down.
entries.proof_pairing: COGS/GP% customer results — tracking whether contracted bean prices follow the futures move
entries.caveats: SECONDARY SOURCE (Trading Economics aggregating ICE futures) — the only non-primary entry in the register; replace with a primary series if one becomes fetchable. Exchange price in USD, not the roasted/contracted price UK operators pay — GBP/USD and roaster contract lags sit between the two. Futures remain historically elevated despite the y/y fall. Global series, equally relevant to Ireland accounts in principle, but scoped UK-only pending a decision on IE duplication. Vertical is a coarse proxy — prefer hand-matching to the account's actual menu.
